title: 2025 Supplemental Poverty Measure: what Census reported, and what threshold growth did to it
subject: Census's 2025 Supplemental Poverty Measure rates by age, housing tenure and state, PolicyEngine's recomputation of them from the 2026 CPS ASEC public-use file (with finer age groups), and its estimate of what threshold growth beyond inflation did: the 2025 SPM rate at 2024 thresholds grown by CPI-U (12.31 percent, 0.69 points below Census's 2024 rate of 13.0) and by C-CPI-U, and the points that threshold growth beyond CPI-U adds to the 2025 rate (0.80 for all people) by age, tenure and state.
search_terms: SPM thresholds rose faster than inflation
SPM 2025 poverty rate if thresholds adjusted only for inflation
how updating annual poverty thresholds affects poverty rates 2024-2025

thresholds_anchored_cpiu.description: The post's counterfactual: 2025 SPM poverty with each tenure group's national base threshold set to its corrected 2024 BLS value grown by CPI-U (32,649/31,812, 1.02631); the equivalence scale, the geographic adjustment and every unit's resources stay at their published 2025 values. The baseline is the published 2025 SPM.

thresholds_anchored_ccpiu.description: The post's chained variant: as thresholds_anchored_cpiu, with the 2024 bases grown by C-CPI-U (1.0248, an eleven-month 2025 mean).

thresholds_anchored_fcsuti.description: Census SEHSD-WP2026-22's headline counterfactual: the corrected 2024 SPM thresholds inflated to 2025 by BLS's FCSUti price index (3.44 percent; Table A.1: $40,581, $34,011 and $40,570). The post publishes no figure in this world.
